subject: Request: Atlas Health — MFN & Benchmark Clause (exec risk mitigation)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Cho <sarah@atlashealth.io>, Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@atlashealth.io>
Date: 2028-11-22T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas Health — MFN + benchmark ask (need exec mitigation & signoff)

Team — looping you on a sticky ask from Atlas. Highlights:
- ARR committed: $2.4M year 1 (50% prepay).
- Customer is requesting an MFN clause across our US commercial customers and a benchmark clause that lets them reset pricing if their competitors demonstrate lower per-token cost within 180 days. They also asked for a 12-month regional preference (preferred vendor in Northeast markets).
- Discount: 35% off list for first 12 months (volume-based step-down after), plus a three-month pilot at a further 10% pilot credit.

Why this is high risk: MFN + benchmark create open door to price parity requirements and force us to lock pricing across segments; the regional preference verges on an exclusivity signal. Legal flagged as "high-risk commercial restrictions."

Customer rationale: Atlas is scaling fast in Medicare advantage analytics. They want predictable unit economics and a written safety valve if competitors undercut. Their procurement team is pushing hard; we have momentum on product integration and a committed POC start Dec 4.

I propose we escalate for an exec risk mitigation instead of a flat refusal. Suggested mitigations to propose to Atlas:
1) Convert MFN to a narrow "most-favored named competitors" clause limited to direct clinical analytics vendors (list to be agreed), and capped to our published SMB pricing tier only (not enterprise blends).
2) Benchmark clause: allow a single-price-adjustment request in the first 120 days, requiring independent evidence (public pricing or signed 3rd-party quote) and a minimum revenue delta to trigger. Any adjustment would be capped at 5% and take effect prospectively.
3) Remove any exclusivity language; offer a "preferred vendor" statement with no market carveouts and a 30-day termination right.
4) Pilot credit to be limited to $60k and applied as one-time invoice credit after pilot acceptance.
5) Add a rollback mechanism: price protection with a minimum 12-month guaranteed revenue threshold; if not met, pricing reverts to our standard list.

Attachments: term sheet v3 and forecast from the AE.

As this impacts long-term commercial protections, I need signoff from Deal Desk + one exec (Rishi or Marissa) to present the mitigated language to Atlas. Can one of you greenlight the mitigation approach or propose alternatives?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. I reviewed the term sheet and agree this is high-risk from a commercial guardrails standpoint. Two immediate asks from Deal Desk/Legal:
1) Remove any undifferentiated MFN that can bind our public SMB pricing; the carve to "named competitors" is reasonable but must be strictly defined with a short sunset (6 months).
2) Benchmarks: require a higher bar for evidence and a longer contention window to reduce churn engineering. 120 days seems short; propose 180 days, a 10% minimum claimed price delta, and independent verification.

Marissa will escalate to Pricing Committee for a formal deviation approval if execs want to proceed with the mitigations you outlined.

I also want to surface potential revenue impact modeling — Ben, please run sensitivity for a 5% rollback vs 10% within next 4 hours.

Marissa Cole

Quick numbers from sensitivity:
- Scenario A (5% prospective cap, 120d evidence window): expected present value of revenue over 24 months drops by ~2.7% (~$65k net) given our expected usage uplift.
- Scenario B (10% cap + 180d): PV drop ~5.8% (~$140k).
- If MFN is allowed to apply to public SMB list pricing the downside could be material over Q1-Q2; worst case we see a 12% ARR erosion in similarly-sized accounts over 12 months due to repricing cascades.

Recommendation: accept narrow named-competitor MFN with 6-month sunset, benchmark limited to one validated claim in 180 days, cap at 5%, and pilot credit limited to $60k. Require Atlas to sign an explicit non-disclosure on any competitive pricing they submit for benchmarking.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Team — I appreciate the proposal and Ben’s modeling. From an executive risk/finance perspective I will provisionally approve the mitigation approach with caveats:
- MFN must be explicitly scoped to the named competitor list and exclude any customers on multi-year committed reserved capacity contracts.
- Benchmark price-reset: allow a single upward or downward adjustment request, evidence must be external and signed by a CFO at the competitor or public pricing tied to a dated offer; adjustment capped at 5% and applied prospectively starting next billing cycle.
- Pilot credit capped at $60k and applied as a one-time invoice credit after acceptance criteria are met; no automatic roll-forward.
- Add a clause: if Atlas requests price parity within 12 months for subsequent deals, requests are subject to an independent review and approval by Redwood Pricing Committee.

I need Legal to produce final redlines reflecting these guardrails. If Legal marks as acceptable, Marissa please confirm and I’ll sign the exec deviation. Jordan — hold customer conversation until we have redlines (aim EOD tomorrow).

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
